media_epithet.notes: ANALYTICALLY DISTINCT FROM EVERY OTHER EPITHET IN THIS DATASET. 'Green River Killer' and 'Golden State Killer' were assigned by the press from geography; 'The Killer Clown' from an unrelated hobby. This one was coined by the offender himself, in communications sent to media and police, and then adopted by the press. Recording it is not endorsing it — but the fact that a self-assigned label became the standard designation is a finding about how these cases are narrated, and it is the same appetite for attention that ended the case.

birth_date.notes: Commonly given as 9 March 1945. No record retrieved. The ages stated in the ABA Journal account — 29 in 1974, 59 at arrest in 2005 — are consistent with a 1945 birth year, but that is inference from reported ages, not a record, and is not asserted here.

convictions.notes: IMPORTANT: the guilty plea was NOT a bargain to avoid execution. The offences fell between 1974 and 1991; Kansas adopted its current capital statute afterwards, so the death penalty was never available for these counts. This distinguishes the case sharply from USA-002-RIDGWAY and USA-004-DEANGELO, where the plea purchased life. Accounts describing Rader as having 'escaped' the death penalty by pleading are wrong: there was nothing to escape.

last_known_offence.notes: Fourteen years then elapsed between the final charged offence and arrest, during which he was not offending and was not suspected. Compare USA-004-DEANGELO, whose desistance ran 32 years. Both cases show that cessation of offending is not evidence of incapacitation, death or relocation — the standard assumptions when a series stops.

detection_delay_factors.value: The offences spanned 1974 to 1991 and arrest followed in 2005. Rader was not identified by investigative work during the offending period and was not a suspect. The case was closed by his own decision to resume communication with police in 2004, thirteen years after the last charged offence, at a point when no investigative avenue was converging on him.

detection_delay_factors.notes: A FIFTH DISTINCT DELAY MECHANISM, and the only one in the dataset that was not resolved by investigation at all. Bundy: jurisdictional fragmentation. Ridgway: institutional neglect plus forensic limits. DeAngelo: absent technology. Gacy: an unconnected conviction record. Rader: none of these — the investigation had not solved it and, on the retrieved record, was not going to. He surfaced. Any analysis of detection using this dataset must treat this case as a censored observation rather than a success, or it will overstate what investigative capability achieved.

identifying_evidence.value: Metadata in a deleted word-processing document on a floppy disk sent to a television station in February 2005. The file properties recorded that it had last been saved by a user named Dennis, and associated the disk with Christ Lutheran Church and the Park City library.

forensic_methods_used.value: Document metadata analysis, followed by confirmation through familial DNA comparison. The reference sample was a stored medical specimen taken years earlier from an adult relative at a university clinic, obtained by legal process.

forensic_methods_used.notes: SAME DISTINCTION AS USA-004-DEANGELO, and it arises three years earlier here. Neither method is scientifically unreliable; both raise governance questions. The relative whose stored medical sample was used was not a suspect, was not asked, and had provided the specimen for clinical care. This dataset names neither the relative nor the specimen type: the analytic point is that a third party's medical record became an identification tool, and that point survives without exposing her. Compare the consumer-genealogy pathway in DeAngelo — different mechanism, same underlying question about whose biological information becomes available to an investigation, and on what authority.

method_now_disputed.notes: No technique relied on here has been found scientifically unreliable. Null by design; the governance concerns are recorded under forensic_methods_used, because a contested method is not a discredited one.

interrogation_method.value: Investigators used deception during the communications phase. Rader asked whether a floppy disk could be traced; police answered through a newspaper advertisement that implied it could not. He sent the disk, and it identified him. He referred to that exchange in interview as the thing that undid him.

sources.citation: American Bar Association Journal. 'How the Cops Caught BTK: Playing to a serial killer's ego helped crack the case.'

interrogation_method.notes: Documented investigative deception that worked. Recorded without endorsement: the same family of techniques, applied to a suggestible subject in a custodial setting, produced the confession problems documented in USA-003-HALL and the false confessions in docs/investigative-failures.md. What differs here is that the deception induced an act producing independent physical evidence, not a statement. That distinction — deception that generates evidence versus deception that generates admissions — is the one worth carrying into any analysis of interrogation tactics in this dataset.

confession_reliability.value: Not load-bearing for the convictions, which rest on physical and documentary evidence including his own communications. His extensive post-conviction statements from custody are a separate matter and are treated as unreliable.
